title: Alerd Berd Health Response v1
description: Contract returned by a monitored service at its health route (default GET /health). Alerd Berd polls this route and derives UP, DEGRADED or DOWN. Only status is required; a minimal service may return {"status":"ok"}.

status.description: The service’s self-reported health and primary status source. Once a response arrives and parses, Alerd derives status from status, components and metrics; the HTTP code only determines whether a response arrived. Monitor-side fallbacks can worsen the result, never hide a failure.

version.description: Running service version (e.g. SemVer), displayed for information.

uptimeSec.description: Process uptime in seconds since its last start.

timestamp.description: Response timestamp (ISO 8601, UTC), used to detect stale or frozen responses.

runtime.description: Optional, additive in v1: actual runtime and framework versions in the serving process. Read at runtime, e.g. node_modules/next/package.json, rather than dependency ranges or build-time constants. Alerd checks npm releases and GitHub advisories and shows package health separately from availability. Include only in protected spec-health, never public liveness.

node.description: Process Node.js version (process.versions.node), without a leading v.

commit.description: Git commit of the running build, 7 to 40 hex characters. In Coolify enable Advanced > Build > Source commit availability > Available during build, and forward SOURCE_COMMIT from ARG to ENV in the Dockerfile. This proves the deployed versions of all packages in that commit’s lockfile and confirms Alerd updates exactly.

packages.description: npm package name to exact installed SemVer, e.g. {"next":"16.4.5"}. Alerd evaluates the packages selected for monitoring on the service.

components.description: Service subsystems (database, cache, external API). A down component makes the monitor red; degraded makes it amber.

detail.description: Short plain-text explanation, stored in Incident.cause when DOWN.

metrics.description: Numeric measurements with optional thresholds. Value ≥ warn means DEGRADED (amber); value ≥ crit means DOWN (red). If thresholds are omitted, configured monitor fallbacks apply when set.

unit.description: For example ms, MB, %, or count.

warn.description: Threshold for DEGRADED (amber). Default direction: higher is worse.

direction.description: above (default): values above the threshold are bad. below: values below it are bad, e.g. free disk space.
